Nested-batch detection uses `batchDepth` alone, but `activeRoot` is cleared before the outer `doc.update()` finishes committing/publishing — a re-entrant `batch()` in that window silently runs unbatched
findings.evidence: `batch()` sets `this.activeRoot = null` in the inner `finally` (line 84) while `this.batchDepth--` only runs in the outer `finally` (line 89), i.e. after `doc.update()` returns. Yorkie commits the change and publishes its events *inside* that call, so during publish `batchDepth === 1` but `activeRoot === null`. Any `batch()` re-entered from a listener takes the nested short-circuit (line 67) and runs `fn()` with no ambient update; each `editText` then falls to `withUpdate`'s else-branch (line 126) and opens its own `doc.update` re-entrantly inside the outer update's publish — breaking the "one batch = one undo unit" invariant the whole design rests on, and committing a Yorkie change from inside Yorkie's own event dispatch. The two state variables (`batchDepth`, `activeRoot`) are not kept in sync; the nested check should test `activeRoot` (the thing `withUpdate` actually keys off), not the depth counter.

findings.summary: `store.batch()` now wraps every docChanged ViewUpdate, so a purely remote update opens a real `doc.update()` re-entrantly inside Yorkie's own event dispatch (applyChangePack / history.undo publish)
findings.evidence: `update()` calls `this.store.batch(...)` before the `Transaction.remote` filter, so remote-only updates — which previously did literally nothing — now enter `YorkieNoteStore.batch` (yorkie-note-store.ts:78) and call `this.doc.update(...)`. That dispatch chain is reached *from inside* Yorkie: `history.undo()` → publish → `subscribeRemote` listener → `view.dispatch` → this plugin update. Correctness rests entirely on the body being empty (no change committed). It also adds a new throw surface on a path that previously could not throw: `Document.update` throws for a removed document, and an exception thrown from a ViewPlugin `update()` makes CodeMirror destroy the plugin, after which local edits never reach the CRDT again (silent data loss). Cheapest fix: only open the batch when at least one transaction survives the filter.

findings.summary: `NoteEditorAPI.undo()/redo()` bypass the read-only guard that both keyboard paths apply
findings.evidence: The history keymap is deliberately left unbound on a read-only mount (`const historyKeymap: Extension = readOnly ? [] : keymap.of([...])`, line 213) and the vim route explicitly checks `cm.cm6.state.facet(EditorView.editable)` (line 52), but the returned API's `undo`/`redo` call `runHistory('undo'|'redo')` → `store.undo()` unconditionally with no `readOnly` check. Any host that calls `api.undo()` on a read-only mount writes to the Yorkie document (notes-view.tsx:95 passes `readOnly` through). Today the only caller, notes-toolbar.tsx:210, is hidden behind `canFormat = !readOnly && ...`, so it is unreachable from the UI — but the guard is one call site away from being defeated.

findings.summary: The `undoFloor` depth comparison is invalidated once Yorkie's undo stack hits its bounded depth, which per-keystroke granularity now reaches quickly
findings.evidence: `canUndo()` compares `doc.getUndoStackForTest().length > this.undoFloor`. Yorkie's internal history is a bounded stack (it evicts the oldest entry past its max depth). With the new granularity (one CodeMirror transaction = one undo unit, i.e. roughly one keystroke — see docs/design/notes/notes.md:304), that bound is reached in normal typing. Once entries are evicted from the bottom, the absolute depth no longer identifies the seed: the floor blocks `undoFloor` real user edits instead of the seed, so the oldest surviving edits become permanently un-undoable. A floor expressed as an absolute stack length only works while nothing is evicted.

findings.summary: MemNoteStore undo/redo emits a whole-document `replace`, which wipes selection/cursor state in the mounted editor
findings.evidence: `undo()`/`redo()` emit `{ type: 'replace', content: this.text }`; note-sync's `applyRemote` turns that into `changes: { from: 0, to: view.state.doc.length, insert: change.content }` (note-sync.ts:34). Replacing the entire document collapses the user's selection and drops the caret to a mapped position, whereas the Yorkie store's undo emits targeted `edits`. Any non-collaborative (MemNoteStore-backed) mount therefore loses the caret on every undo. Emitting a minimal diff, or at least preserving the selection on the replace transaction, would match the Yorkie path.

findings.summary: The vim `u` / `<C-r>` route skips the toolbar refresh that `runHistory` performs
findings.evidence: The keymap and API paths go through `runHistory` (line 205), which calls `selectionCb?.(computeActiveFormats(view.state))` precisely because the store's depth changed and the resulting transaction may not be observed. The vim route (line 53) calls `store[kind]()` directly, so when an undo produces no document change (Yorkie's undo returns early when no ops applied) no `docChanged` update fires and the toolbar's `canUndo`/`canRedo` (notes-toolbar.tsx:193, refreshed only from `onSelectionChange`) stays stale.

findings.summary: `CodeMirror.commands.undo/redo` are patched process-wide at first `initialize()` and never restored
findings.evidence: `defaultVimHistory` snapshots the originals at module evaluation and `routeVimHistoryToStore()` overwrites the shared `CodeMirror.commands` map permanently (no restore in `dispose`). Any other consumer of `@replit/codemirror-vim` in the same bundle inherits the note-store routing (it falls through only when the view has no `noteStoreFacet`), and if `CodeMirror.commands.undo` were ever undefined at import time the fallback `defaultVimHistory[kind](cm)` would throw rather than no-op.

+# Notes native undo — lessons (issue #604)
+
+## Context
+
+Migrate WaffleNotes undo/redo from CodeMirror local history to Yorkie
+`doc.history`, so undo preserves peers' concurrent edits.
+
+## Lessons
+
+- The issue's prerequisite spike resolved cleanly: `Text.edit()` reverse
+  ops are supported on `@yorkie-js/sdk` 0.7.13. The `Tree.editByPath`
+  merge caveat that motivated the spike is a Tree-only limitation and
+  never applied to notes, whose whole content is one `Text`.
+- An empty `doc.update()` pushes nothing onto the undo stack, so
+  `batch()` does not need to pre-check whether the body will mutate.
+- Disabling `basicSetup`'s `history()` silently breaks vim's `u` /
+  `<C-r>` too: `@replit/codemirror-vim` routes them through
+  `CodeMirror.commands.undo/redo`, which call `@codemirror/commands`'
+  `undo(view)` and no-op without the history extension. The static
+  `CodeMirror.commands` map is read at call time, so overriding it is
+  the supported-shaped hook; its `:undo` ex-command copy is snapshotted
+  at module load and cannot be re-routed.
+- Undo granularity changes: CM history groups keystrokes by time
+  (`newGroupDelay`), Yorkie's unit is one change. One CM transaction =
+  one undo unit, so undo now steps per keystroke — the same behavior
+  Docs and Slides already have after their migrations.

+# Notes native undo — migrate to Yorkie `doc.history` (issue #604)
+
+PR: (to be filled after opening)
+
+## Goal
+
+Move WaffleNotes undo/redo off CodeMirror's local history onto
+Yorkie-native undo (`doc.history`), so undo carries CRDT semantics and
+preserves a peer's concurrent edits instead of last-write-wins-ing over
+them. Reuses the pattern already shipped in Slides
+(`docs/design/slides/slides-native-undo.md`) and Docs
+(`packages/frontend/src/app/docs/yorkie-doc-store.ts`).
+
+## Prerequisite spike (done — result recorded here)
+
+Verified against the pinned `@yorkie-js/sdk` 0.7.13 that character-level
+`Text.edit()` **is** reversible through `doc.history`:
+
+- Two `content.edit()` calls inside ONE `doc.update()` push exactly one
+  undo-stack entry; `history.undo()` reverts both, `redo()` re-applies.
+- The undo emits a `local-change` event with `source === 'undoredo'`
+  carrying `edit` ops on `$.content` with correct `from`/`to`/`content`
+  (already reversed in apply order), i.e. the dormant `isUndoRedo` path
+  in `yorkie-note-store.ts` receives exactly what it needs.
+- A `doc.update()` whose body mutates nothing pushes **no** undo entry,
+  so an empty batch is free.
+
+(`Tree.editByPath` merge non-reversibility, called out in the issue,
+does not apply — notes store markdown in a single `Text`.)
+
+## Approach
+
+**Store layer (`packages/notes/src/store/store.ts`)** — extend
+`NoteStore` with `batch(fn)`, `undo()`, `redo()`, `canUndo()`,
+`canRedo()`. Undo becomes store-owned (like `DocStore`/`SlidesStore`)
+rather than view-owned.
+
+**`YorkieNoteStore`** — ambient-root + `withUpdate()`: a top-level
+`batch()` opens ONE `doc.update()` and every `editText()` runs against
+that ambient root, so one CodeMirror transaction group = one Yorkie
+change = one undo unit. `setLocalSelection` folds into the batch's
+ambient presence proxy when a batch is open. `undo()/redo()` delegate to
+`doc.history`, gated by an undo floor captured at construction (after
+`ensureText()` seeding) so a user cannot undo the seed away.
+
+**`MemNoteStore`** — snapshot-based local history so the engine still
+has working undo without a CRDT (tests / non-collaborative use). Undo
+emits a `replace` remote change so the view reflects it, mirroring how
+the Yorkie store's undo comes back through `subscribeRemote`.
+
+**`note-sync.ts`** — wrap the per-`ViewUpdate` `editText` loop in
+`store.batch()`.
+
+**`editor.ts`** — `basicSetup({ history: false, historyKeymap: false })`;
+bind `Mod-z` / `Mod-Shift-z` / `Mod-y` to the store (skipped in
+read-only); `NoteEditorAPI.undo/redo/canUndo/canRedo` delegate to the
+store. Vim's `u` / `<C-r>` go through `CodeMirror.commands.undo/redo`,
+which the vim adapter looks up at call time — override them once to
+route to the note store resolved from the view's `noteStoreFacet`, else
+vim undo would silently no-op with CM history disabled.
+
+## Tasks
+
+- [ ] `NoteStore`: `batch` / `undo` / `redo` / `canUndo` / `canRedo`
+- [ ] `MemNoteStore`: snapshot history + `replace` emission on undo/redo
+- [ ] `YorkieNoteStore`: ambient root, `withUpdate`, batch, undo floor,
+      `doc.history` delegation
+- [ ] `note-sync.ts`: wrap local edits in `store.batch()`
+- [ ] `editor.ts`: disable CM history, history keymap → store, API
+      delegation, vim command routing
+- [ ] Tests: batch grouping = 1 undo unit, undo floor, peer-edit
+      preservation (churn regression), no-echo on undo, MemNoteStore
+      history, engine-level keybinding
+- [ ] `docs/design/notes/notes.md`: Yorkie-native undo section
+
+## Out of scope
+
+- Time-based keystroke coalescing (Yorkie's undo unit is the change;
+  Docs and Slides behave the same way).
+- `:undo` / `:redo` ex-commands in vim (the vim package snapshots those
+  handlers at module load, so they cannot be re-routed).
